subject: Benchmarking run plan for Skyline Payments onboarding - acceptance criteria and artifacts
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Menon <rajesh.menon@skyline-payments.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmarking run plan for Skyline Payments onboarding - acceptance criteria and artifacts

Hi Rajesh —

Thanks again for the sync last week. Attached is a compact benchmarking run plan we propose for the onboarding acceptance window. Aim is to validate both throughput and P99 tail latency under your expected peak profile and a 20% burst. High-level: 

- Goals / acceptance gates: sustained 250 reqs/sec (50 token average) with median latency < 120ms and P99 < 450ms for generation endpoints; embeddings pipeline < 40ms P95 per vector.
- Test types: steady-state throughput run (30m), burst stress (3x for 5m), prefix-cached run, and a low-latency smoke.
- Artifacts we will produce: raw metrics CSV, per-request traces for sample window, config we used (attached), and a short runbook explaining how to reproduce locally.

Can you confirm the target traffic profile (average tokens per request and concurrent user model) and whether we should run against your staging VPC or use our dedicated test harness?

Attachments: skyline_load_script_v1.py (load script), redwood-config-skyline.json (runtime config)

If the plan looks good I’ll schedule the run for Wednesday morning PST and loop in Monica and Ben to execute and capture artifacts.

Thanks,
Mateo
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Rajesh Menon <rajesh.menon@skyline-payments.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@skyline-payments.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking run plan for Skyline Payments onboarding - acceptance criteria and artifacts

Thanks Mateo — this looks sensible and focused. Quick answers: 

- Traffic profile: most requests average ~48 tokens; heavy checkout flows spike to ~120 tokens but are only ~5% of load. Concurrent users translate to roughly 220 rps average, 320 rps peak during promotions.
- Staging preference: please run against our staging VPC (staging-01) — that's network-isolated and mirrors production routing. We'll provision a temporary ingress rule for Redwood's test harness.

Can you also include a brief checklist for test preconditions (API keys, warm cache steps) so our infra team can validate beforehand?

Also attaching a short sample of our request stream (anonymized).

Regards,
Rajesh
Sr. Platform Engineer, Skyline Payments
[Attachment: skyline_request_sample_anon.json (application/json)]
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Benchmarking run plan for Skyline Payments onboarding - acceptance criteria and artifacts

Team — forwarding Rajesh's confirmation and request. Action items before Wednesday run: 

1) Ben: can you prepare the harness to run from our east-us cluster but poke Skyline's staging-01 via the temporary rule? Include an option to replay their sample stream.
2) Monica: please draft the precondition checklist Rajesh asked for (API keys, TLS cert thumbprint, KV-cache warm steps, expected tokenization). Keep it one page.
3) Marissa: will need a tracing window 09:00-11:00 PT on Wed; can you reserve collectors and ensure sampling is enabled for P99 capture?

I’ll coordinate the calendar invite once Ben confirms the harness parameters. Keep notes in the deal thread in Redwood app (linked).

Onwards —
Mateo
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 07:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Benchmarking run plan for Skyline Payments onboarding - acceptance criteria and artifacts

Quick update from infra: harness ready. Outline below — confirm and I’ll kick off at 09:15 PT Wed.

- Runner: east-us-2 dedicated node pool (3 instances, 2xA10G equiv)
- Traffic generator: replay of skyline_request_sample_anon.json with token distribution mapping; steady-state 30m @ 250rps, then 5m burst at 720rps, then 10m cool-down.
- Probing: 1s pacing for latency samples; detailed traces collected for 1% of requests and full traces for 100% in a 60s sample window to capture P99 tail.
- Preconditions checklist: API key for staging (scoped to run), confirm per-ip ingress rule, warm cache step (10m warm at 50rps), and confirm model variant pin (gpt-redwood-2-medium-quant).

Attachments: skyline_load_script_v1.py (already provided)

If Monica can confirm the checklist and Rajesh confirms ingress by 08:30 PT, I’ll start the run at 09:15 and push artifacts to the shared Drive link.

-Ben
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Menon <rajesh.menon@skyline-payments.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking run plan for Skyline Payments onboarding - acceptance criteria and artifacts

Hi all — checklist and quick pre-run notes below (kept concise for infra team):

Preconditions (to verify by 08:30 PT):
- Staging API key: provided to bench-runner@redwood.ai (scoped to read/generate).
- Ingress rule: staging-01 permits test harness IP range 35.203.44.0/24.
- Model pin: gpt-redwood-2-medium-quant (confirmed).
- Tokenization expectations: avg 48 tokens, spike pattern included in sample.
- Warm cache: run 10m at 50rps before measurement window.

Success criteria (for this acceptance):
- Sustained 250 rps steady-state (30m) with median latency < 120ms and P99 < 450ms.
- Burst handling: system degrades gracefully; error rate < 0.5% during 3x burst.

Post-run deliverables (within 90 mins):
- benchmark_results_20260603.csv (per-request latencies)
- run_summary.md (actionable bullets + any anomalies)
- traces (1 full 60s window and sampled traces)

I’ll be on the call to validate metrics and tag anomalies. Good luck — ping me on Slack if any infra hiccups.

—Monica
Customer Success Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Rajesh Menon <rajesh.menon@skyline-payments.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking run plan for Skyline Payments onboarding - acceptance criteria and artifacts

Hi team —

Thanks for a clean run and rapid artifacts. Findings summary: 

- Steady-state: achieved 255 rps sustained; median latency 98ms; P99 420ms.
- Burst: brief degradation observed at minute +2 of burst (P99 ~ 730ms) but error rate stayed at 0.32% and recovered within 45s.
- Observations: cold-starts on rare path where KV cache miss on large-embedding requests contributed to tail.

We consider the run acceptable against our acceptance gates with the following simple follow-ups: 
1) Redwood to provide recommended cache warm policy for large-embedding flows.
2) Schedule an action item to reduce burst tail to <600ms — proposed canary of a larger instance type for peak windows.

Artifacts received and stored at drive link. We'll move forward with the onboarding sign-off pending the two follow-ups above.

Thanks,
Rajesh
Sr. Platform Engineer, Skyline Payments
[Attachment: benchmark_results_20260603.csv (text/csv)]
